Power = points better than an average FBS team on a neutral field, from scoring plus opponent-adjusted team stats and the emphasised factors. Off and Def are scoring ratings in points. Home field is each team's own extra (or missing) home edge on top of the league average. A team that missed the spread by 21+ last game (green) is a Vegas-overreaction candidate.

Backtest by season

SeasonGamesPredictive missVegas missBoth agreeStrongPredictive 3+Reactive 2+Models split

FBS vs FBS, graded against the closing line; 52.4% breaks even at standard odds. Every game is predicted from earlier games only. The reactive model's weights for each season were fit only on earlier seasons. The predictive model's blend weights were tuned on 2022–25, so its numbers for those seasons (and anything that uses it) flatter it; 2010–21 and 2026 are the fair test. Models split is graded on the predictive model's side.

  • Scoring ratings. Each team has an offense and a defense rating in points, adjusted for opponent and home field, starting from a preseason prior (last season, roster talent, returning production) that fades as games come in. Recent games count more; blowouts past 30 are mostly ignored.
  • Team stats. Ten opponent-adjusted stats (EPA per play, yards per play, rushing and passing EPA, explosive plays, first-down rate, run-stuff rate, line yards, special teams, penalties) are blended with the scoring rating by a regression fit on 2022–2025 FBS games.
  • Factors (after 3+ games): wins over preseason expectation, turnover margin, rush rate, and how the market reacted to last week's result.
  • Predictive model = everything above combined into its own line, without looking at the betting line. This is the model line shown for every game.
  • Reactive model starts from the sportsbook line and adjusts it by what the same inputs say the market tends to miss (fit on 2008–2025 games, the last 4 seasons counted fully and older ones a little less each year back). Its edge is how far it moves off the line.
  • Home field. League average plus each team's own home edge from its previous 14 seasons, pulled toward average.
  • Both agree = the predictive model is 5+ points off the line and the reactive model 1.5+ on the same side. 2010–2025 against closing lines: 463–385 (54.6%); 2010–21 alone 52.9%.
  • Strong = a predictive 3+ edge where the market just overreacted the other way (your side missed by 21+ last game, or the opponent covered by 21+), lines under 28. A "look closer" flag: 982–900 (52.2%).
  • Models split = the predictive model is 5+ off the line but the reactive model leans 1.5+ the other way. The predictive side went 117–129 (47.6%), so treat its edge with caution.
  • Line move compares the first DraftKings line pulled for the game (usually Monday's) with the latest one (live while the page is online). From 2012–2021 opening lines, the line moved toward the predictive model's 5+ point picks 63% of the time.
  • Lines are the DraftKings spreads pulled when this page was built. They don't change after that.
  • Live scores for this week's games come from ESPN's public scoreboard while the page is open and online, refreshed every minute during games. Offline, the page works the same without them.
  • Defense Dog tags a home underdog with a top-25 defense (model rating at kickoff), from week 5 on. Tested on 2010–2026 closing lines, these teams covered 136–143 (49%), so the tag is tracked, not used in the model lines; past weeks show how they did.
  • Fan attitude is the mood of the week's coverage of each team (local papers, beat writers, fan sites) from Google News headlines in the 7 days before the week's games: the share of positive vs negative headlines, 50% = neutral. Game-result words are ignored, since the model already has the results. It is tracked only, not used in the model lines.
  • Past weeks show what both models would have said before each game, using only games played earlier, graded against the closing line. Pick = the side the predictive model liked against that line.
  • Win % assumes the final margin lands within about ±16 points of the model line two times out of three.
